Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demos last week. The execs want a short written plan confirming the Dedicated capacity sizing that maps to the committed throughput in our SOW. High-level ask: verify that Redwood can support our steady-state and peak bursts so we can schedule the Hosted->Dedicated migration without service risk.

Quick context:
- Expected steady: ~3.2M tokens/day (~37 reqs/sec average, median 85 tokens per request)
- Peak bursts: up to 6.5M tokens/day for campaign spikes (brief 2–3 hour windows)
- p95 latency target after migration: <= 350ms for interactive calls
- Business go-live target: earliest weekend of Sept 10–12 (flexible)

Can you confirm what validation steps you need from us (data samples, representative prompts, load window) and a timeline for sizing sign-off + cutover rehearsal? I attached our throughput workbook for reference.

Also include any SLA exception requests or required procurement milestones so legal can sync.

Celine
Director of AI Platform
Nebula AI

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Celine Park <celine.park@nebula.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput commitment + target go-live - sizing assumptions and test plan

Celine / Karthik — putting the initial technical assumptions and a lightweight test plan in one place so procurement/engineering can align.

Sizing assumptions:
- Baseline model: redwood-xl (float16 execution with Q4 quantization path)
- Average tokens per call: 90 (we'll validate with your samples)
- Concurrency target for steady-state: 150 concurrent requests (gives ~3.2M tokens/day)
- Burst concurrency: up to 420 concurrent requests (covers 2–3 hour spike)
- GPU target: H100 80GB preferred (A100 fallback available)
- Node packing: expect ~48–64 concurrent inference slots per H100 depending on batch tuning
- Initial pool recommendation: 8 x H100 for dedicated pool (staging) => scales to 14 x H100 for full production buffer if acceptance shows higher peak efficiency needs

Validation tests (staging run):
1) Functional smoke (run basic prompts, check outputs + model parity)
2) Steady-state soak — 72h at average concurrency profile; collect p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, KV cache hit rates
3) Burst ramp tests — scripted 2–4 hour ramps to peak concurrency, check throttling, queue depth, and fallback to hosted if configured
4) Failure injection — simulate a node OOM and validate automatic routing/fallback behavior

Acceptance metrics (pass/fail):
- p95 latency <= 350ms across 72h soak
- No more than 0.3% requests with server errors during soak
- KV cache effectiveness reduces token throughput by at least 20% for repeated prefixes (if applicable)
- GPU utilization under 90% average (headroom for autoscaling)

Runbook highlights for cutover:
- Canary window: route 5% traffic for first 30 minutes, ramp to 25% by 2 hours, to 100% by end of day if metrics are green
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 500ms, error rate > 1%, or autoscaler thrash > 10% within 30m
- Pre-cutover warm-up: 12–24h of synthetic traffic to pre-populate KV caches and JIT kernels

I'll put a more detailed node-count calc in the staging checklist doc and share links.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Celine Park <celine.park@nebula.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput commitment + target go-live - canary and validation cadence

Celine — a few operational details to lock down the weekend and avoid surprises.

Canary & rollout cadence (recommended):
- T-3 days: staging validation complete; install telemetry hooks and alerts
- Day 0 (cutover start): deploy dedicated pool in target region; run 12h warm-up with synthetic traffic (target 60% of steady)
- Canary step 1: 5% production traffic for 30m, evaluate p95/p99, error logs, tail latencies
- Canary step 2: 25% for 2h, run a scripted burst to validate autoscaler response
- Canary step 3: 60% overnight, full switch next morning after business hours if stable

Rollback and mitigation playbook (short):
- Immediate rollback: if any primary metric crosses rollback threshold, route traffic back to Hosted API pool and alert on-call
- Graceful degradation: auto-fallback to a smaller model variant for non-critical routes to preserve throughput with slightly higher latency

Operational requirements from Nebula:
- Confirm IP allowlist for Dedicated control plane access (we need a CIDR range)
- Provide final doc with sample prompts (20 examples) and a list of routes you want in the initial cutover
- Identify on-call contacts for weekend window (primary + backup)

I'll also prepare a staging validation checklist (md) and share via Drive. We recommend a 72-hour soak in staging once your tests are complete — this catches kernel JIT warm-up and cache behavior.

Laura Bennett
Platform Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

[attachment: staging_validation_checklist.md]
